title: Audit Storage & Retention Orchestrator: adaptive tiering, partitioning, and RBAC signal enrichment
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Summary
We need an orchestration layer (Audit Retention Orchestrator) on top of the audit streaming pipeline that: (1) enriches events with RBAC v2 context and SSO/SAML admin signals at ingest time; (2) applies tenant- and sensitivity-aware TTLs and tiering policies; (3) partitions and compacts indexes to reduce storage costs while maintaining fast lookup for security investigations and compliance exports. This ticket defines the design, implementation plan, rollout strategy, and runbook for the first-phase implementation.

Goals
- Attach RBAC v2 metadata (role hierarchy, admin flag, scope) to auth-related audit events during enrichment so retention decisions are deterministic and queryable.
- Ensure SSO/SAML lifecycle events (IdP config changes, certificate rotation, user-provisioning) are flagged as high-sensitivity with longer retention by default.
- Implement adaptive tiering: hot (7d low-latency index), warm (30–90d compressed index), cold/archival (S3 Glacier-ish) with automated movement based on policy and query heat.
- Partition indexes primarily by tenant + date + sensitivity bucket to avoid hotspotting and reduce query fanout.
- Enforce per-tenant storage spend caps and soft/ hard quotas with billing alerts and automatic retention acceleration when budgets are exceeded.

Design decisions and trade-offs (current thinking)
- Enrichment at ingest vs post-process: choose ingest-time enrichment (lightweight lookup to RBAC cache) to avoid later backfills and to make retention deterministic. Trade-off: slightly higher ingest latency; mitigated by an in-memory RBAC snapshot service and async fallback.
- Partition keys: use composite key [tenant_id | sensitivity | yyyy-MM-dd]. This avoids large single-day partitions for heavy tenants. We will evaluate based on initial tenant distribution; may add hash-shard for top 5% tenants.
- Indexing: maintain a small secondary metadata index (tenant+sensitivity->partition pointers) to speed compliance searches. Secondary index is compact, updated with partition lifecycle ops.
- Cost model: prefer storage-smart compression (delta+LZ4) in warm tier rather than aggressive deduplication to retain queryability for forensics. Archival to cold storage is irreversible (longer restore time) and requires export tooling.

Architecture sketch
- Ingest stream (kinesis/kafka) -> Enrichment worker pool (adds rbac_v2 roles, admin_flag, idp_event_tag) -> Router/Policy engine (evaluates policy rules/TTL based on tenant profile and sensitivity) -> Write to appropriate tier/partition (hot-index shard or warm compressed blob or cold-archive job metadata).
- Sidecar services: RBAC Snapshot Service (cached, auto-refresh on RBAC changes), Quota Controller (per-tenant spend accounting), Tiering Controller (moves partitions on schedule/trigger), Compaction Service (background compaction jobs).

Implementation plan (phases)
1) Prototype ingest enrichment (2 sprints): wire up RBAC snapshot read, enrich auth events, write to staging index. Add unit tests and basic query hooks.
2) Policy engine and simple TTL (1 sprint): support tenant policies, sensitivity buckets, and assign partition tag at ingest. Integrate with billing to surface soft quota.
3) Tiering controller + compaction (2 sprints): implement warm-tier writes and scheduled compaction jobs + metadata index.
4) Cold archival & restore (1 sprint): export job to cold store, restore path, and update Console export UI.
5) Rollout & hardening (1 sprint): canary to 5% tenants -> 25% -> 100%. Full runbook and incident playbook.

Rollout and safety
- Canary: start with internal tenants and low-volume customers. Use shadowing to verify retention assignment without changing storage path for first canary.
- Metric thresholds: ingestion latency increase > 12% or enrichment error rate > 0.1% -> auto-rollback.
- Backfill strategy: for existing data we will run a scheduled reindex job that re-evaluates sensitivity using RBAC snapshot, but only for retained date ranges required by compliance (configurable). Backfill must be throttled to avoid query impact.

Operational runbook (high level)
- On enrichment errors: mark event as 'sensitivity_unknown' -> route to warm tier with 14d TTL and create async retry. Notify infra channel.
- When a tenant exceeds soft quota: send billing notification; on hard quota breach: trigger retention acceleration (reduce TTLs for non-sensitive buckets) and notify Customer Success.
- Restore pathway: for cold-archived partitions, create restore request which schedules restore prefixed task and updates metadata when available. Expected RTO: hours for full restore; minutes for selective export.

Testing and validation
- Load tests simulating top 5% tenants (ingest amplification) to validate partitioning and compaction.
- Chaos tests: RBAC snapshot expiry and enrichment fallback.
- Cost model validation: compare simulated monthly spend pre/post-tiering with real compressed sizes.

PRs, specs, and artifacts
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Audit+Retention+Orchestrator (working draft)
- GH prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4923 (enrichment + policy engine initial)
- Query/console mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_example_console_mockups
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Audit+Retention+Runbook

Open questions / blockers
- RBAC snapshot TTL: how often should snapshot service refresh to avoid stale retention decisions? (Design suggests 5m by default.)
- Export compliance: required export formats for EMEA/regulatory customers; need legal input on minimum retention durations for SSO events.
- Cold storage provider SLA: confirm restore RTO options and costs across cloud providers.

Recent progress notes (updates)
- 2025-02-12: prototype enrichment added to staging pipeline; ingest latency increased by 3% in perf tests; acceptable. (Aisha)
- 2025-02-20: RBAC Snapshot Service schema v2 approved by Security (PR #4961). Added caching and watch hooks for RBAC v2 changes. (Liam)
- 2025-02-27: Policy engine initial rule DSL merged to platform:rules. GH PR #5004. Needs broader rule set review from Compliance. (Rafael)
- 2025-03-03: Tiering controller design doc uploaded; compaction strategy (time-window + tombstone purge) sketched. Planning compaction PoC next sprint.

Review requests and reviewers
- Please review: enrichment latency trade-offs and RBAC snapshot TTL (ping @security-eng)
- Reviewers: Priya Saini (Security), Markus Vogel (Storage), Sonia Patel (Compliance)
- Slack channels: #security-logs, #infra-ingest, #cost-ops

Acceptance criteria
- Enrichment success rate >= 99.9% at target ingest QPS with <10% median latency overhead.
- Tenant-level retention policies evaluate deterministically at ingest and are visible in Console.
- Warm-tier storage savings >= 30% vs naive hot-only retention for typical customers.
- Runbook and rollback steps documented and rehearsed in one tabletop exercise.

Notes: This ticket is intentionally broad and will be decomposed into multiple sub-issues for implementation tasks (ingest-enrichment, policy-engine, tiering-controller, compaction-jobs, archival-restore). Sub-issues will be linked once scoped.
